title: Thresholded Phase Demultiplexer for Latency‑Bounded Fairness
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: tenant requests show long-tail latency spikes when large prefill requests collide with high-throughput decode workloads. Current phase splitters make binary decisions (prefill vs decode) and simple priority buckets; this causes starvation for latency-sensitive tenants or unnecessary throughput loss for background workloads.

Goal: design and implement a Thresholded Phase Demultiplexer (TPD) that dynamically splits incoming work into micro-phases based on per-request latency budgets and token-credit buckets, while propagating kernel-selection and attention-sparsity hints into scheduling decisions. The TPD should achieve SLO compliance for latency-sensitive tenants (P99 latency target), maintain overall throughput within 5% of baseline, and provide measurable tenant-level fairness (max 3x variance in median latency across tenants with equivalent SLAs).

Scope: scheduling layer changes in the serving runtime that perform: (1) per-request phase thresholding (assign micro-phases A/B/C depending on latency headroom and prefill size), (2) demultiplexing into multiple concurrent queues with adaptive token-credit replenishment, (3) kernel hint propagation so kernel selector can prefer fast kernels for latency phases, and (4) attention-sparsity estimator signals to prefer sparse-attention fastpaths when applicable. Implementation includes scheduler, telemetry, simulation harness, and an A/B rollout path.

Out-of-scope: model architecture changes, quantization engineering, and non-runtime client-side batching strategies.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler implements thresholded demultiplex logic that classifies requests into at least three micro-phases based on latency budget and token estimate.
End-to-end P99 latency for latency-sensitive tenant class meets configured SLOs in canary region under mixed load in stress tests.
Baseline overall throughput degradation <= 5% on our standard benchmark when TPD is enabled.
Per-tenant fairness metric (median latency variance across tenants with same tier) reduced to <= 3x compared to the pre-TPD baseline.
Kernel selector receives and uses phase-level hints in >95% of scheduled decisions in experiments.
Monitoring dashboards (route/model/tenant) surface phase distribution and token-credit utilization.
Canary rollout completes with automatic fallback to previous scheduler on any SLO regression >10% within 2 hours.
Design doc, simulation results, and performance regression PRs merged and code reviewed by runtime and infra owners.
implementation_notes: Phase classification: compute request latency_headroom = configured_slo - observed_queue_latency - expected_decode_time; thresholds: headroom > 120ms => Phase A (latency-priority), 40ms < headroom <= 120ms => Phase B (balanced), headroom <= 40ms => Phase C (throughput-priority).

Token-credit buckets: maintain per-tenant token credits that refill on a moving-average schedule; spending rate controlled by phase (A spends minimal tokens per microbatch, C allows larger microbatches).
Demultiplexer queues: implement three lock-free queues with adaptive admission control; use watermarks computed from current GPU kernel latency estimates and KV cache hit rates.

Kernel hint propagation: attach 'phase_hint' and 'attention_sparsity_score' metadata to requests; kernel selector uses phase_hint to bias toward lower-latency kernels (e.g., fused fastpath) when Phase A.

Attention sparsity estimator: lightweight estimator that samples recent token attention maps and uses model metadata to compute sparsity_score in [0,1]; threshold >0.6 enables sparse-attention fastpaths.
Hedging/fallback: for A-phase requests with tight headroom, schedule speculative small microbatch on fast kernel and cancel larger competing decode if latency target is met early.
Telemetry: emit per-request fields: phase_assigned, headroom_ms, kernel_used, kv_cache_hit, tokens_processed, tenant_credit_before/after. Ensure labels to group by tenant_id and route.
Configuration knobs: phase thresholds, credit refill rate, speculative batch size, kernel preference weights. Expose via runtime config and Console feature flag for canaries.
Simulation: extend existing scheduler-sim harness to model headroom dynamics, kernel latencies for different seq-lens, and attention sparsity distributions per model.
test_plan: Unit tests for phase classification under boundary conditions (exact 120ms/40ms headroom).
Load tests in the simulation harness with mixed tenant profiles: 20% latency-sensitive, 60% standard, 20% bulk. Verify P99 SLOs in latency-sensitive group.
Integration tests with kernel-selector to confirm phase hints change kernel choices deterministically in test mode.
Chaos tests: throttle KV cache and inject sudden prefill storms to validate hedging and fallback behavior.
A/B canary across two regions: 5% of traffic initially, ramp to 25% if no SLO degradation for 24h, then 100% for controlled release.
Regression suite comparing throughput and cost-per-token against baseline for the standard benchmark workloads.
rollout_plan: Step 1: Merge feature-flag-gated code behind Console flag and internal runtime toggle; run unit and integration tests in CI.
Step 2: Internal canary in staging with synthetic mixed load; verify telemetry and dashboards for 48h.
Step 3: Region canary (us-west-2): route 5% production traffic, monitor SLOs, tenant credit drift and kernel usage for 24h.
Step 4: Incremental ramp to 25% over 48h if stable. If any P99 regression >10% or throughput drop >7%, rollback and open incident runbook.
Step 5: Full rollout with phased knob tuning (credit refill, phase thresholds) and 2-week observation window.
Fallback: runtime will support instant rollback to prior scheduler and a dry-run telemetry-only mode to compare decisions without affecting scheduling.
